full_judgment:
10. Mr Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, took me to the judgments of the Courts below and submitted that both the Courts below failed to appreciate the scope and application of section 6 of the Rin Salishi Ain (Act No. 15 of 1989) and erroneously decreed the suit declaring the plaintiffs title and allowed the prayer for khas possession. He further submitted that during pendency of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 137 of 1991 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) the suit itself was premature and incompetent. He further submitted that the plaintiffs having failed to challenge the legality and validity of the order dated 3-12-1990 passed by the Rin Salishi Board, Dakope in Miscellaneous Case No. 187 of 1989 and 188 of 1989 and having not challenged the propriety of the said orders the Court of appeal below was not justified in maintaining a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession as against the defendants. He submitted that the order impugned in this Rule is liable to be set aside. He prayed for an interference by this Court. 

 15. The kabala deed dated 17-5-1982 and 31-7-1983 has been admitted into evidence as being Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 1(ka). Admittedly, the land transferred by Exhibit 1 and 1(ka) attract the provision of section 6 of the Act Admittedly, the valuation of Exhibit 1 and 1(ka) are Taka 12,000 and Taka 13,000 respectively. Admittedly the cases being Nos. 187 of 1989 and 188 or 1989 was filed within 6(six) months from the date of constitution of the Rin Salishi Board. On perusal of the Exhibit 1 it appears that the transfer was made for সাংসারিক খরচা ও অন্যান্য দেনা পরিশোধের জন্য which very much satisfies the requirement of section 6 of the Act but Exhibit 1 (ka), the purpose of selling of the land has not been mentioned. So, apparently the defendant Nos. 15 and 16 lawfully presented the cases before the Rin Salishi Board as per law and the Rin Salishi Board entertained those cases having jurisdiction as per Statute. Admittedly, the Rin Salishi Board allowed those cases and handed over possession in favour of the defendant Nos. 15 and 16 on 27-6- 1991 and admittedly, the plaintiff has preferred M is cellaneous Appeal No. 137 of 1991 and 138 of 1991 and those appeals are pending. Whether the notices were served or not by the Rill Salishi Board upon the plaintiffs are the questions of fact and that were not challenged in the suit. The plaintiff has neither challenged the legality and validity of the orders passed by the Rin Salishi Board nor sought any relief against those orders. From the judgment of the learned Assistant Judge it appears that he disbelieved exclusive possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and held the possession of the defendant in the suit land to be illegal possession. The appellate Court also held the defendant's possession in the suit land to be illegal possession. From the evidence of the PW I it appears that he has substantiated his prayer in his evidence saying. আমরা স্বত্ব প্রচার ও নিষেধাজ্ঞার ডিক্রী প্রার্থনা করছি।” Save and except this prayer there is no other evidence on record to show that he made a prayer for recovery of khas possession as against the defendants. The orders of the Rin Salishi Board passed in above- named two cases have been exhibited as being Exhibit Ka(1) and Kha(1). From Exhibit Ka(1) it appears that notice of the case being No. 187 of 1989 was duly served upon the plaintiff Thereafter, they failed to adduce any evidence and accordingly, the Board being satisfied allowed that case in view of the Article 6 of the Ordinance. So also, it appears from the Exhibit Kha(1) that notice upon the plaintiff was duly served by the Rin Salishi Board and the plaintiff of the instant suit sought for adjournment and thereafter they failed to adduce evidence and ultimately, the case was allowed by the Board after satisfying Article 6 of the Ordinance. It further appears that delivery of possession was admittedly made in favour of the defendants by the Soard on 27-6-1991. This being the position the plaintiffs' suit was not maintainable as it stands framed. The Board was constituted as per a valid statute and the Board was in existence on the date of passing of the orders in those two cases. From the evidence on record, it shows there is not a single piece of evidence to show that the Board had no jurisdiction to entertain those two cases and had no jurisdiction to allow those cases. 

 17. Mr Hasan Foez Siddique although argued that the Board had no jurisdiction to entertain those cases but failed to show anything from the material on record in support of his contention, The requirement of section 6 being found positive in favour of the defendants and the orders passed by the Rin Salishi Board having not been challenged in the suit and in absence of a clear case of coram non judice the plaintiffs were not entitled to file a suit for declaration of title, restitution of possession and permanent injunction. The vires of the Ordinance having not been challenged and pending decision of appeals being Nos. 137 of 1991 and 138 of 1991 pending before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) the plaintiffs were not at all entitled to file the suit. The suit was not at all maintainable. Both the Courts below have miserably failed to consider this aspect judicially. Moreover, admittedly the possession of the suit property having been delivered in favour of the defendants, the plaintiffs were not entitled to file a suit for declaration of title, and recovery of khas possession without challenging the legality and validity of the orders passed by the Rin Salishi Board in those cases. Moreover, the plaintiffs having failed to seek for recovery of khas possession in their deposition the suit Was not liable to be decreed. Both the Courts below have committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in decreeing the suit and also in maintaining the decree passed by the trial Court. I find merit in the Rule.
